items.title: Keith Ingham interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997
items.q: Charlie Parker and somebody else, I think Kenny Dorham or somebody playing there, and Al Haig, and Tatum playing intermission piano, and the joint was empty?

ctx.x: Yeah. But I did come over to the States, you know the only way you could get over was playing the piano on board a trans-Atlantic liner, and they had some of those left and I got a job on that and came over and that was nice. That’s how most of the British guys, the musicians could get over to America and get to New York and hear the music. I remember Bruce Turner, a wonderful sax player who’s dead now, he said he came to New York, he got off the ship, went into this little joint on 52nd Street, and he said it…
